interactions.summary: The reading of Provenzano Salvani becomes Jiang's occasion to argue that a single genuinely good act can matter redemptively, though he immediately qualifies this by stressing the flexibility and severity of purgatory rather than a simplistic last-minute formula.

claims.claim: Jiang interprets Salvani's humiliating public act on behalf of a friend as proof that one remembered good deed can become spiritually decisive against a life otherwise marred by sin.
Jiang draws the radical theological conclusion that hope of salvation remains open even after a terrible life, because God remembers genuine turning rather than only accumulated failure.

When challenged with a Catholic repentance formula, Jiang refuses simplification and says the routes into purgatory are broader and more flexible than people assume, but entry still demands total commitment once inside.
Jiang interprets the posture of moving bent and low on the terrace as Dante's bodily practice of humility after the temptation of pride.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns one late good act into a startling doctrine of remembered redemption.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it will be remembered and it will redeem you
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It intensifies the lecture's insistence that hope is never fully foreclosed.

signature_moments.moment: Purgatory is described as easy to enter relative to hell but brutal to inhabit because it requires endless committed labor once admitted.
signature_moments.source_phrase: once you're in, you have to work really, really hard
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It prevents the redemption argument from collapsing into cheap grace.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture refines the free-will and hope account by stressing both the breadth of purgatory's entry conditions and the severe discipline of life within it.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang is drawing a broad interpretive lesson from Dante rather than laying out a formal Catholic doctrine; the packet should preserve that as lecture synthesis rather than doctrinal precision.
